arStrings.szText: There is one oft-overlooked aspect of this tome: its shared authorship, between Deckard and his ward.

For Cain, Leah offered a second chance at fatherhood. While her dark parentage would make her of great interest to any Horadrim, Deckard adopted her simply because she needed a loving guardian and a safe home.
Our duty to Sanctuary comes before our blood. But Deckard may have found the one exception to this rule. Leah became his family—yet his rearing of her would also guide Sanctuary’s future.
I am only thankful he died before he could see the fate that befell her.
